issues.body:
`crates/sparq-shaclc/src/raw/shaclc12.rs` and `shaclc12ext.rs` are generator output (`//! GENERATED by @rdf-shuttle/gen-rs from shaclc12ext.shuttle — DO NOT EDIT.`). This PR reformats both (~12.9k insertions / 4.0k deletions across the two).

`scripts/regen-shuttle-parsers.sh` contains no rustfmt/`cargo fmt` invocation (grep for `fmt|rustfmt` returns nothing). So after this PR the checked-in artifacts are no longer byte-reproducible from the generator, and the first person to follow the documented procedure — `crates/sparq-shaclc/tests/provenance_drift.rs` literally instructs "regenerate, do not hand-edit" — will produce unformatted output that fails the now-hard `cargo fmt --all --check`.

This is a foreseeable CI breakage created by this PR's own gate flip, on a path the repo explicitly tells contributors to regenerate. It does not red today (provenance_drift.rs only checks the grammar SHA-256 pin and the header/DO-NOT-EDIT marker, not artifact content), which is precisely why it will be discovered at the worst time.

Note `ignore = [...]` in rustfmt.toml is NOT an option here: it is a nightly-only key and rustfmt.toml documents a stable-options-only rule.
issues.fix_hint:
Pick one and land it in this PR (it is the PR that creates the hazard):

(a) Add a formatting step to `scripts/regen-shuttle-parsers.sh` after the artifacts are written, e.g. `rustfmt --edition 2021 crates/sparq-shaclc/src/raw/shaclc12.rs crates/sparq-shaclc/src/raw/shaclc12ext.rs` (or `cargo fmt -p sparq-shaclc`), so regeneration is fmt-clean by construction and the artifacts stay reproducible.

(b) Alternatively, revert the two `src/raw/*.rs` files to the generator's exact output and add a file-level `#![rustfmt::skip]` immediately under the `//!` header in each (tool attributes are stable), keeping the artifacts byte-identical to generator output and out of the gate.

(a) is preferable: it keeps the whole tree uniformly formatted and keeps the DO-NOT-EDIT contract truthful. Either way, add one line to the drift test or the script's header comment recording that generated artifacts must be fmt-clean.
issues.title: Generated DO-NOT-EDIT parser artifacts reformatted, but the regen script gains no fmt step — the next regeneration reds the new hard gate

issues.body:
Token-stream comparison of all 642 changed files isolates 4 .rs files whose diff is not producible by rustfmt. None is mentioned in the PR description or the commit messages. All four are behaviour-preserving as far as I can verify, but they defeat the reviewability contract of a 642-file mechanical PR (reviewers and tooling assume "formatting only").

1. `crates/sparq-engine/src/lib.rs` — test renamed `order_by_mixed_timezones_matches_lenient_order` -> `order_by_mixed_timezones_matches_total_order`, and the assertion message changed from "ORDER BY dateTime must match the total temporal order" to "...through the temporal cache must match the total order". Provenance is the concern: merge-base `dece4ca1`, PR branch tip `1a167090`, and main `b19db765` ALL have `_lenient_order`. The new name appears only in the merge commit `dc1a2468` ("fix: merge main into #3581 to resolve conflicts"), i.e. on neither parent. That is the signature of a conflict resolution that rewrote content rather than taking a side. I confirmed the test body and the `want` array are byte-identical to main's, and grep finds no other reference to the old name, so nothing is lost — but a merge that invents content is worth an explicit look.

2. `crates/sparq-geo/tests/reproject.rs` — see the separate minor issue.
3. `crates/sparq-mcp/src/solid.rs` — see the separate minor issue.
4. `crates/sparq-conformance/src/inference/dl_suite.rs` — a `//` comment reworded/reordered (rustfmt does not rewrap comments; `wrap_comments` is nightly and unset).
issues.fix_hint:
Either revert these four hunks so the diff is provably `rustfmt`-only, or keep them and say so explicitly in the PR body ("also renames <test>, moves <assert>, reformats <comment>") so a reviewer knows the token-stream is not invariant.

For (1) specifically, confirm the rename was intentional rather than a merge artefact: re-run the conflict resolution taking main's side for `crates/sparq-engine/src/lib.rs` and re-apply `cargo fmt`, then diff. If the rename IS wanted (the doc comment above the test does describe a total order, so the new name reads more accurately), land it as its own one-line commit with a message, not inside a conflict resolution.

Reproduce the audit with: lex both revisions, drop comments and `,`/`{`/`}`/`;`, and compare token sequences — every other file is either identical or a pure `use`/`mod` permutation.
issues.title: Non-formatting code edits inside a mechanical rustfmt PR — one introduced by the merge commit and present on NEITHER parent

issues.body:
This PR correctly rewrites the OpenSSF `warnings_strict` row to say the `fmt + clippy (gate)` job hard-gates `cargo fmt --all --check`. But the sibling SSDF evidence table was not updated and now asserts the opposite of reality:

`compliance/ssdf/evidence.md:31`
`| \`ci.yml#clippy\` | clippy \`-D warnings\` (gating) + fmt (non-blocking today) | PO.3.2, PW.5.1, PW.7.2 |`

After this PR that statement is false. This is a compliance artifact, and the PR itself is what invalidated it — the same reason the openssf file needed the edit. It is an understatement rather than an overclaim, so it is not a certification-integrity failure, but it is precisely the doc-honesty drift the repo's own conventions call out, and it makes the two evidence files disagree about the same CI job.

Second, smaller instance of the same class: `bench/dict/README.md:87` still refers to "The CI `clippy (gate) + fmt` job", a job name that no longer exists after the rename in this PR. (`docs/branch-protection.md` WAS correctly updated, and I confirmed the rename is otherwise safe — `.github/advisory-registry.json` has no `lint` entry so check-advisory-registry.py C4 stays green, and the old name in `scripts/check-advisory-registry.py` / `scripts/tests/test_ci_summary_gate.py` is synthetic fixture data, not a live binding.)
issues.fix_hint:
In `compliance/ssdf/evidence.md`, change the row to match the openssf wording, e.g.:

`| \`ci.yml#lint\` (`fmt + clippy (gate)`) | \`cargo fmt --all --check\` (gating) + clippy \`-D warnings\` (gating) | PO.3.2, PW.5.1, PW.7.2 |`

and fix the stale job name in `bench/dict/README.md:87` to `fmt + clippy (gate)`.

While there, grep once more for any remaining claim that fmt is deferred/informational:
`grep -rniE "fmt.*(non-blocking|informational|deferred|not gat)" --include='*.md' .`
That query currently returns exactly the one SSDF hit.
issues.title: Compliance evidence updated in one place only — compliance/ssdf/evidence.md still states "fmt (non-blocking today)"

issues.body:
The `assert_eq!(epsg_code(&Crs::Other("http://www.opengis.net/def/crs/EPSG/0/27700".into())), Some(27700));` statement is relocated from after `assert!(proj4_definition(99999).is_none());` to immediately after the `#[cfg(not(feature = "epsg_full"))] assert!(proj4_definition(2056).is_none());` line. rustfmt never reorders statements, so this is a hand edit.

I checked the hazard that matters here: the two `#[cfg]` attributes still attach to the same statements they did before (the insertion lands after the `cfg(not(...))`-attributed assert and before the `cfg(epsg_full)`-attributed one), so neither cfg is retargeted, and all the statements are independent pure assertions. Behaviour is unchanged in both feature states.

Flagged only because it is invisible noise in a diff whose reviewability depends on being mechanically generated.
issues.fix_hint: Restore the original statement order (keep the rustfmt line-wrapping) so the file's diff is formatting-only, or call the move out in the PR body. If the intent was to group the `epsg_code` assertions, do that in a separate commit.
issues.title: An assertion statement is moved, not reformatted, inside `unsupported_crs_errors_are_explicit`

issues.body:
In the `method not found` arm, the PR branch rewrites `format!("method not found: {other}")` to `format!("method not found: {}", other)`. rustfmt does not perform this transformation in either direction — it is a hand edit (or an errant lint autofix).

Output is byte-identical, so there is no behaviour change. It is also not a new clippy-gate risk: the `format!("...{}", var)` shape already occurs ~460 times across `crates/`, and main is green under the workspace `-D warnings` clippy gate, so `clippy::uninlined_format_args` is evidently not firing on the CI toolchain. I checked for a suppression and found none in-tree (only `vendor/spargebra/Cargo.toml` sets `uninlined_format_args = "warn"`), so this is a latent inconsistency if that lint ever tightens.

The correct rustfmt output for this hunk would have kept the captured identifier.
issues.fix_hint:
Restore the captured-identifier form and let rustfmt wrap it:

```rust
other => Err(RpcError::new(
    METHOD_NOT_FOUND,
    format!("method not found: {other}"),
)),
```

This keeps the file's diff formatting-only and stays on the inlined-arg side that the rest of the module uses.
issues.title: Inline format arg un-inlined: `format!("...{other}")` -> `format!("...{}", other)`

issues.body:
The job is renamed to `fmt + clippy (gate)`, but the `rustfmt (check)` step is appended at the very end of the `lint` job, after `clippy` (default features), `clippy --all-features`, both `cargo doc` passes, and the standalone `bench/dict` clippy + selftest.

`cargo fmt --all --check` needs no compilation and finishes in seconds. Running it last means a PR whose only defect is formatting burns the full multi-build lint job before reporting — the most expensive possible way to surface the cheapest possible failure, on a gate that (by construction of this PR) will now fire regularly while contributors adapt.
issues.fix_hint:
Move the step to be the first step after the toolchain/cache setup, so it matches the `fmt + clippy (gate)` name and fails fast:

```yaml
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@e18b497796c12c097a38f9edb9d0641fb99eee32 # v2
      - name: rustfmt (check)
        run: cargo fmt --all --check
      - name: clippy (deny warnings)
        run: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
```

(`rustup component add rustfmt clippy` already runs above it, so no other change is needed.)
issues.title: `rustfmt (check)` runs last, after four full workspace builds — no fast-fail, and it contradicts the new job name

issues.body:
Recording a scope limit rather than a defect, since this PR promotes fmt to a hard gate.

I could not execute `cargo fmt --all --check` in this environment: the `rustfmt` component is not installed for the 1.88.0 toolchain and `rustup component add rustfmt` fails on a read-only filesystem. So the gate's own green-ness is asserted by CI, not by this review.

One concrete residual risk I could partially bound: main advanced by several commits after the PR branch point, and of the 21 `crates/**/*.rs` files main changed in that window, 10 are NOT in this PR's reformatted set — `crates/sparq-nlq/{src/guard.rs,src/lib.rs,src/link.rs,tests/injection.rs}`, `crates/sparq-reason-el/src/classify.rs`, `crates/sparq-reason/src/datalog/{eval.rs,mod.rs,tests.rs}`, `crates/sparq-rsp/examples/replay_runner.rs`, `crates/sparq-zk-compose/tests/sparql_catalog.rs`. Inspecting them: zero long non-comment lines (the apparent long lines in `classify.rs` are wide-Unicode comments miscounted by byte-length tools), and their `use` blocks already follow the version-One order this reformat imposes (`{as_numeric, ArithOp, Num}`, `{Row, NO_ID}`, `{Concept, Names, Normal, Role, BOTTOM, TOP}`). So they look already fmt-clean — but that is inspection, not `--check`.

Also masked by construction: I ignored `,`/`;`/`{`/`}` to see through rustfmt's punctuation edits, so a one-element-tuple `(x,)` -> `(x)` or an array-repeat `[T; N]` -> `[T, N]` slip would not appear in my token comparison. Both are compile or type errors, so the workspace build+test leg covers that class.
issues.fix_hint: Before arming, confirm the `fmt + clippy (gate)` check is green on the merge commit (not just on an earlier push), since the merge pulled in unformatted-at-the-time main commits. `cargo fmt --all --check` locally on the merge result is the one-command confirmation.
issues.title: Unverifiable in review: `cargo fmt --all --check` cleanliness, incl. 10 files merged from main after the branch point

verdict.summary:
Repo-wide `cargo fmt --all` (642 files) + flip of rustfmt to a hard CI gate. I verified the mechanical claim rather than trusting it: lexing every changed .rs file at base (b19db765) and head and comparing token streams, 551/642 are token-identical modulo `,`/`{`/`}`/`;` and comments; 89 more are permutations explained entirely by `use`/`mod`/`pub use` reordering (version-One order, matching rustfmt.toml `edition = 2021`). Match-arm brace wrapping inside the two touched `macro_rules!` bodies (sparq-shaclc, sparq-core) is in emitted code, not matchers, so it is semantics-preserving. The source-text drift tests that `include_str!` reformatted sources (sparq-trust cert_closure_doc_drift, sparq-introspect schema_diff_feature_off, sparq-shaclc provenance_drift) all still hold. The ci.yml job rename is safe: `.github/advisory-registry.json` has no `lint` entry so check-advisory-registry.py C4 stays green, and ci_summary_gate.py is name-agnostic post-#3773. `bench/feature-off-declarations/3581.json` matches the V2 mechanism and reads honestly.

But exactly 4 .rs files carry edits rustfmt cannot produce, none mentioned in the PR, and one exists on NEITHER merge parent (invented by the conflict-resolution commit). All four are behaviour-preserving, so that is a reviewability/provenance defect, not a correctness one. The blocking gap is completeness: two DO-NOT-EDIT generated parser artifacts were reformatted (~17k lines) while `scripts/regen-shuttle-parsers.sh` gained no fmt step, so the next regeneration reds the very gate this PR hardens; and `compliance/ssdf/evidence.md` still says "fmt (non-blocking today)", falsified here while only the openssf sibling was updated.

Not verified: `cargo fmt --all --check` itself (rustfmt component unavailable, read-only FS). 10 files main changed post-branch-point were not reformatted; they inspect as already fmt-clean.
